resources.title: Explain which part of a tropical storm is the most dangerous and why.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain which part of a tropical storm is the most dangerous and why.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The eyewall is the most dangerous part of a tropical storm. - The eyewall surrounds the eye of the storm. - In the eyewall, hot air rises very quickly. - Rising air creates very low air pressure, which causes the strongest winds in the storm. - There is also very heavy rainfall, which can lead to flooding and damage.

resources.title: Explain which preventative defence failed to increase the impact of Hurricane Katrina and why.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain which preventative defence failed to increase the impact of Hurricane Katrina and why.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The levees in New Orleans were badly designed and failed. - Levee failure caused widespread flooding, covering 80% of the city. - Flooding damaged homes, businesses, and infrastructure. - Roads, bridges, and utilities collapsed, making rescue and aid difficult. - People were trapped and needed emergency shelter. - Secondary effects included homelessness, unemployment, and health risks. - Repairing flood damage was very expensive and long-term. - The failure increased the overall social and economic impact of the storm.

resources.title: Explain why a country moves from the stable population of Stage 1 to the rapid growth of Stage 2 in the Demographic Transition Model.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why a country moves from the stable population of Stage 1 to the rapid growth of Stage 2 in the Demographic Transition Model.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- In Stage 1, the total population does not grow because both birth and death rates are high. - Birth rates are very high because there is high infant mortality, so parents have more babies to ensure some survive to adulthood. - People are often poor and cannot afford contraception. - In Stage 2, countries start to see an improving health system, which means there are more doctors and hospitals. - Death rates are also high because there are little doctors or hospitals and people do not understand how diseases spread. - As a country moves into Stage 2, it sees an improving health system with more access to medical care and better education, which helps people understand how diseases spread. - Diets and nutrition improve as the country gets wealthier, meaning fewer people are malnourished and death rates fall. - However, birth rates stay high because children are still needed to work in agriculture, so the population experiences rapid growth.

resources.title: Explain why a single measure like GNI per head may have limitations, and how the Human Development Index (HDI) provides a clearer view of a country's development.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why a single measure like GNI per head may have limitations, and how the Human Development Index (HDI) provides a clearer view of a country's development.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Development is complex and involves many different parts interacting. - GNI per head is an average for the whole country, which means it can hide inequality between the very rich and the very poor. - A country might get rich from selling oil, but the citizens may not see the money if a corrupt nation embezzles it. - This measure does not tell us about quality of life or health and ignores variations between different regions. - Using multiple measures at once gives a much more accurate picture of progress. - The Human Development Index (HDI) combines different factors, such as life expectancy and literacy and schooling. - It looks at education, healthcare, and income to show how well a country is using its wealth to help people. - The HDI scale ranges from 0 to 1, with 1 representing the most developed countries. - Because HDI covers more than just money, it is a better indicator of overall development.

resources.title: Explain why attrition changes the size and shape of rocks on a beach.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why attrition changes the size and shape of rocks on a beach.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Attrition happens when rocks hit each other in the waves. - The rocks break into smaller pieces. - The edges of the rocks become smoother. - Waves carry the rocks along the beach, causing more collisions. - Over time, rocks become rounded and smaller. - This changes the shape and size of beach material.

resources.title: Explain why birth and death rates are useful indicators of a country's level of development.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why birth and death rates are useful indicators of a country's level of development.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The birth rate is the number of babies born per 1,000 people each year. - LICs (lower income countries) often have higher birth rates because of less access to contraception. - The death rate is the number of deaths per 1,000 people each year. - Infant mortality rate shows how many babies die before the age of one. - Falling death rates usually mean a country has access to safe water and medicine. - High death rates often show a lack of healthcare and food security. - These rates help geographers see if the basic needs of the people are being met.

resources.title: Explain why changing consumer behaviour and reducing food waste are essential for a sustainable food supply.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why changing consumer behaviour and reducing food waste are essential for a sustainable food supply.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The UN says one-third of all food / about 1.3 billion tonnes of food is wasted each year. - Supermarkets often refuse to sell disfigured or ugly vegetables. - If more people buy ugly vegetables from businesses like Oddbox, it can help to stop food waste. - Reducing waste means we do not have to produce as much food, which protects existing ecosystems from being turned into farms. - Consumers can choose to buy seasonal produce that is grown locally from farmers' markets or local businesses to reduce the need to import food from other countries. - Changing to a vegan or low-meat diet is part of permaculture. - Consumers can also choose to buy organic food to protect the soil and water. - All these choices help to create sustainable food supplies.

resources.title: Explain why coastal management has improved safety for people and property at Mappleton, but also caused problems further south.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why coastal management has improved safety for people and property at Mappleton, but also caused problems further south.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Groynes have created wider beaches which absorb wave energy. - Rock armour protects the cliffs from destructive waves, so they erode more slowly and the land is safer. - The village is protected from flooding and people can use the coast without fear of landslides or waves. - Management has reduced risk to property and farmland. - However, Groynes trap sediment at Mappleton, so less sediment is transported south by longshore drift. - Beaches and cliffs south of Mappleton have less protection, which has caused faster erosion in those areas. - For example, Spurn Point has become less secure. - People and animals, like Hebridean sheep, can be washed away.

resources.title: Explain why creating green spaces is important for sustainable urban living.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why creating green spaces is important for sustainable urban living.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Green spaces like Central Park provide areas for people to exercise. - This improves physical well-being, mental health and reduces diseases like obesity. - Parks can help the environment by making air pollution lower. - Trees and grass help to cut surface runoff when it rains heavily, reducing flood risk for people in the city. - Some cities, like Valencia, have a park that runs all around the city. - These spaces create a sustainable lifestyle that can be continued forever.

resources.title: Explain why deposition happens at certain coastlines, and why this results in different types of beaches.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why deposition happens at certain coastlines, and why this results in different types of beaches.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Deposition happens when waves lose energy, usually in shallow water. - Constructive waves break gently and deposit material on the beach because their swash is stronger than their backwash. - The material builds up between the high water mark and low water mark. - The type of beach formed depends on the size of the sediment being deposited. - Sandy beaches are made of small particles of sand. - It is easy for the backwash to move small particles, creating long, wide, and flat beaches. - In contrast, shingle beaches are made of pebbles and larger particles. - Shingle is hard to move with the backwash, so it builds up and forms short, steep beaches compared to sandy beaches. - Areas with high rates of nearby cliff erosion often supply lots of sediment, leading to larger depositional features.

resources.title: Explain why deposition occurs in the lower course of a river.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why deposition occurs in the lower course of a river.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Deposition happens when the river loses energy. - This occurs if the river becomes shallower or the volume of water decreases. - Deposition also happens if the river reaches the mouth. - The river drops sediment like silt, sand, and gravel. - Deposition builds up levees, floodplains, and deltas. - Lower course rivers have gentle slopes so deposition dominates over erosion.

resources.title: Explain why designing sustainable homes can help with energy conservation.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why designing sustainable homes can help with energy conservation.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Designing homes with proper insulation is a key way to conserve energy. - Good insulation means less heat is lost, so less heating is used. - Houses can be built with solar panels on the roof to make electricity. - Some homes use mini wind turbines to provide a source of renewable energy. - Companies like SolarCity encourage homes to have their own battery and energy supply. - This reduces the demand for energy from the national power grid.

resources.title: Explain why earthquakes can happen at all three types of plate margins and what the differences are.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why earthquakes can happen at all three types of plate margins and what the differences are.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Earthquakes happen because of plate movement. - At all margins, pressure builds up due to friction. - At conservative margins, plates slide past each other. - At destructive margins, plates collide and one plate can get stuck. - At constructive margins, plates move apart and tension builds. - The type of movement causes different earthquake patterns.

resources.title: Explain why earthquakes with a magnitude of 7 or higher often cause severe impacts.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why earthquakes with a magnitude of 7 or higher often cause severe impacts.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Magnitude 7 releases a lot of energy. - The shock (seismic) waves are stronger, which makes the ground shake more violently. - The scale is logarithmic. - Shaking lasts longer and can affect larger areas. - Buildings and infrastructure may collapse causing deaths. - Secondary effects such as landslides, tsunamis and liquefaction are more likely.

resources.title: Explain why economic factors make it difficult for some countries to secure an energy supply.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why economic factors make it difficult for some countries to secure an energy supply.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Natural resources are often very expensive to find. - It costs more to dig for oil miles under an ocean than on land. - Many countries have to import oil or gas from other nations. - Price fluctuations make it hard for countries to plan their budgets. - Renewable energy like wind can also be impractical and expensive. - For example, turbines must be switched off if the wind is too strong, which wastes money.

resources.title: Explain why food insecurity can lead to social unrest and political change.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 2 - Resource Provision > Patterns of Food Supply &  Demand > Strategies to Increase Food Supply

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why food insecurity can lead to social unrest and political change.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- When people are starving, they often blame their governments. - History shows this can lead to riots or civil wars. - The French and Russian Revolution occurred due to poor harvests and food shortages. - Some people may stockpile and hoard food. - This makes food insecurity worse for everyone else. - This completely changes how a country is run.

resources.title: Explain why hydroelectric power is an effective but controversial way to increase energy supply.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why hydroelectric power is an effective but controversial way to increase energy supply.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Hydroelectric dams trap water high above the ground. - This water acts as a store of gravitational potential energy. - When the water falls, it rotates a turbine which turns a generator. - It is effective because it is more reliable than wind or solar power. - An example of this is the Hoover Dam in the USA. - However, it is controversial because it changes the paths of rivers. - This can force people to move out of their houses or harm local wildlife.

resources.title: Explain why international agreements are important for mitigating climate change.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 1 - Climate Change > Responses to Climate Change > Evaluation of Mitigation

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why international agreements are important for mitigating climate change.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Climate change is global, so one country acting alone is not enough. - Agreements like the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement set targets for countries to reduce emissions. - These agreements encourage cooperation and monitoring between nations. - Countries can share technology and funding to reduce greenhouse gases. - Meeting targets reduces global temperature rise and protects humans and ecosystems. - Agreements help ensure that long-term mitigation strategies are coordinated worldwide.

resources.title: Explain why international agreements are needed to tackle climate change.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 1 - Climate Change > Responses to Climate Change > Climate Change: Strategies

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why international agreements are needed to tackle climate change.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Climate change is a global problem, so country acting alone is not enough. - Greenhouse gases spread through the atmosphere and affect the whole planet. - Countries work together through international agreements to tackle this issue. - The Kyoto Protocol set emission targets for developed countries to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. - The Paris Agreement aimed to reduce future warming by limiting global temperature rise to below 2°C. - These shared rules and agreements encourage global cooperation and long-term action to reduce climate change.

resources.title: Explain why irrigation and appropriate technology are effective ways to increase food supply.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 2 - Resource Provision > Patterns of Food Supply &  Demand > Strategies to Increase Food Supply

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why irrigation and appropriate technology are effective ways to increase food supply.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Irrigation means watering plants correctly. - Adding water at the right time can increase cereal production massively. - It can take a yield from 1,000kg to 7,000kg per hectare. - In 1998, only 20% of land was irrigated, but it grew 40% of all crops. - Appropriate technology includes effective interventions. - It includes using good farming techniques to stop soil erosion. - Helping farmers water plants correctly is the most effective way to boost supply.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why landfills are unsustainable.

resources.title: Explain why many countries still rely on fossil fuels despite their environmental impact.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why many countries still rely on fossil fuels despite their environmental impact.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Fossil fuels like coal and oil are burnt to heat water and create steam. - The steam turns a turbine which rotates a generator for power. - They can produce power on demand whenever the population needs it. - However, burning them contributes to global warming through CO2. - Fossil fuels are not renewable and inefficient compared to some newer energy sources. - Despite this, the existing infrastructure makes them easy for countries to use.

resources.title: Explain why oceanic plates can sink under continental plates.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why oceanic plates can sink under continental plates.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The Earth's crust is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates. - Oceanic plates are thinner and also younger. - Oceanic plates are made of rock that is much denser and heavier than continental rock. - Continental plates are thicker but made of lighter rock. - When these two plates meet, the denser plate will sink underneath the lighter one. - This process is called subduction.

resources.title: Explain why plate margins are important locations on the Earth’s surface.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why plate margins are important locations on the Earth’s surface.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The Earth is divided into pieces known as tectonic plates which float on the semi-molten mantle. - Plate margins are where two tectonic plates meet. - They are also called plate boundaries. - This is where most of the world's geological activity happens because the plates are in constant movement. - These plates can touch or sit next to each other, leading to processes like subduction where the denser plate sinks. - They are important because they show the interaction between oceanic plates and continental plates.

resources.title: Explain why pressure builds up at destructive and conservative plate margins.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why pressure builds up at destructive and conservative plate margins.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Plates are made of rough rock. - Plates catch against one another . - At destructive margins plates push together. - At conservative margins plates slide past. - Plates can lock. - Pressure builds until release.

resources.title: Explain why recent climate change cannot be explained by one single cause.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 1 - Climate Change > Natural & Human Causes of Climate Change > Climate Change: Human Influence

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why recent climate change cannot be explained by one single cause.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Climate change has many interacting causes. - Natural factors include orbital changes and volcanoes. - These explain past climate change. - Recent warming is too fast for natural causes alone. - Human activities increase greenhouse gases. - Humans burn fossil fuels, adding large amounts of CO₂. - Farming releases methane, a strong greenhouse gas. - Climate change today is caused by a combination of factors, mainly human ones.

resources.title: Explain why rivers have different energy levels in the upper, middle, and lower courses.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why rivers have different energy levels in the upper, middle, and lower courses.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- In the upper course, rivers have steep slopes so water moves fast and has high energy. - In the middle course, the gradient is gentle so water moves slower and energy is moderate. - In the lower course, the slope is very gentle so water moves slowly and energy is low. - High energy in the upper course causes vertical erosion. - Moderate energy in the middle course causes both erosion and deposition. - Low energy in the lower course causes deposition and lateral erosion.

resources.title: Explain why scientists use multiple methods to study climate change.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 1 - Climate Change > Natural & Human Causes of Climate Change > Climate Change: Evidence

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why scientists use multiple methods to study climate change.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- No single method covers all timescales. - Ice cores show climate over hundreds of thousands of years. - Tree rings and pollen show climate over thousands of years. - Temperature records give detailed recent data. - Using multiple methods improves accuracy and reliability. - Methods can cross-check each other to confirm patterns of climate change. - Together, they show long-term and short-term trends.

resources.title: Explain why secondary effects of volcanic eruptions can be more widespread than primary effects.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why secondary effects of volcanic eruptions can be more widespread than primary effects.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Primary effects happen close to the volcano. - Secondary effects can spread far from the eruption. - Volcanic ash and gases can cause volcanic winter, reducing crop yields far away. - Lahars and mudflows can destroy settlements and farmland downstream. - Volcanic activity can trigger flooding and tsunamis, affecting coastal areas. - Damage to roads, ports and transport can disrupt the economy over a wide area. - Businesses may lose income and tourism declines, spreading economic impacts nationally or internationally.

resources.title: Explain why soils in tropical rainforests are infertile despite rapid plant growth.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why soils in tropical rainforests are infertile despite rapid plant growth.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Rainforests receive very heavy rainfall. - Rain washes nutrients away from the soil, this process is called leaching. - Most soil is infertile. - Only a thin top layer has nutrients. - Plants grow fast because nutrients are recycled quickly.

resources.title: Explain why some High Income Countries (HICs) have entered Stage 5 of the model.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why some High Income Countries (HICs) have entered Stage 5 of the model.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Stage 5 occurs when the birth rate falls below the death rate. - Birth rates are very low because of equality of access to education. - Women often choose to have fewer children or none at all. - There is very low infant mortality so parents know their children will live. - Good healthcare systems mean people live much longer into old age. - This leads to natural decrease where the total population begins to decline.

resources.title: Explain why some areas with high tectonic risk still attract large populations.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why some areas with high tectonic risk still attract large populations.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- High fertility of volcanic soils attracts farmers. - Jobs and economic opportunities in cities may outweigh risk. - Some people are born in the area and cannot move easily. - Good governance and emergency planning make living safer. - Cultural and family ties mean people stay close to home. - Tourism or industry in volcanic regions can create jobs and income.

resources.title: Explain why some earthquakes cause more damage than others, referring to different aspects of an earthquake.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why some earthquakes cause more damage than others, referring to different aspects of an earthquake.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Earthquakes with a higher magnitude release more energy. - The focus is where the pressure is released underground. - Earthquakes with a shallow focus usually cause more damage at the surface. - The epicentre is the point on the surface above the focus. - Areas closer to the epicentre experience stronger shaking and more destruction. - The strength and type of seismic waves affect how much buildings and infrastructure are damaged.

resources.title: Explain why some plate margins experience more frequent earthquakes than others.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why some plate margins experience more frequent earthquakes than others.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Some margins have constant plate movement. - Conservative margins involve continuous friction. - This causes frequent pressure build-up. - Pressure is released in small earthquakes. - Other margins release energy less often.

resources.title: Explain why sustainable sources of meat and fish are important for future food security.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why sustainable sources of meat and fish are important for future food security.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Over-fishing can harm fish populations, similar to how overgrazing harms soil. - We need to protect fish populations so they do not run out. - Some businesses are now growing artificial meat in laboratories. - Grain-fed beef has a lower carbon footprint than grass-fed. - Finding sustainable meat sources reduces damage to the planet. - It helps ensure we can still produce protein without ruining the land.

resources.title: Explain why the Earth’s crust is broken into tectonic plates.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why the Earth’s crust is broken into tectonic plates.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The crust is a thin outer layer of the Earth. - It sits on the semi-solid mantle below. - Heat from the hot core warms the mantle. - This heat causes slow movement in the mantle. - The moving mantle pulls and pushes the crust. - This causes the crust to break into tectonic plates.

resources.title: Explain why the Holderness coast is so vulnerable to erosion.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why the Holderness coast is so vulnerable to erosion.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The coast is made of boulder clay which is soft and easily eroded. - Heavy rainfall can cause mass movements in the cliffs. - There are strong prevailing winds creating destructive waves. - Eroded material is transported away leaving more cliff exposed. - Waves hit the coast frequently and powerfully. - This combination of soft rock, heavy rainfall and strong waves makes Holderness very vulnerable.

resources.title: Explain why the distribution of energy consumption is uneven across the world.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why the distribution of energy consumption is uneven across the world.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Energy consumption is unevenly distributed because of differences in wealth. - Developed countries with rich energy reserves consume far more than less developed countries. - Some people in low-income countries may have no electricity in their homes. - Geography also plays a part, as colder climates require more energy for heating. - For example, large industrial nations like China and the USA need more power for factories. - This creates a gap between energy-rich and energy-poor nations.

resources.title: Explain why the mantle is important for plate movement.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why the mantle is important for plate movement.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- The mantle surrounds the core, which is the hottest part of the planet. - It is made of semi-molten rock that has a thick, liquid-like consistency. - This means the mantle can flow slowly. - Heat from the core creates movement in the mantle through convection currents as the molten rock rises and falls. - The crust floats on the mantle and is broken into tectonic plates. - As the mantle moves, it moves tectonic plates, causing them to shift and meet at plate boundaries.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why the transition to renewable energy can be difficult for a country with energy insecurity.

Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**

**Indicative content**
- Setting up new renewable energy systems is expensive and can cause energy shortages. - A country might suffer from power outages during the change. - Despite this, having a sustainable supply is a long-term advantage. - It stops a country from being dependent on foreign oil or gas. - Using biofuels is an option, but can cause environmental costs. - Balancing economic costs with energy needs is a major challenge.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why tropical storms can have major economic impacts on affected areas.
content.markScheme:

Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**

**Indicative content**
- Transport links like airports and railways can be damaged. - Flights and trains are cancelled, which stops people going to work. - Businesses may have to close. - Crops and livestock can be destroyed, which causes food shortages. - Repairs to buildings and roads are very expensive. - Recovery can take many years.

resources.title: Explain why tropical storms can last for one to two weeks.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why tropical storms can last for one to two weeks.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Tropical storms are very large systems, hundreds of kilometres wide. - Tropical storms are powered by warm, moist air rising over oceans. - As long as storms stay over warm water, energy is replaced, which keeps strong winds and rain going. - The storm only weakens when it moves over land or cooler water, which allows storms to last many days.

resources.title: Explain why tropical storms form over certain parts of the ocean.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why tropical storms form over certain parts of the ocean.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Tropical storms need sea temperatures of 26.5°C or higher to provide energy. - Warm water evaporates and rises, forming low pressure and clouds. - Rising air cools and condenses, releasing energy which strengthens the storm. - Tropical storms usually form in areas with small differences in wind speed at different heights to allow rotation. - These conditions are found in tropical oceans but not near poles where water is too cold.

resources.title: Explain why volcanic activity can cause short-term climate change.
resources.topicPath: Geography: Cambridge International GCSE (2027 Exams) > Paper 1 - Climate Change > Natural & Human Causes of Climate Change > Climate Change: Human Influence

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why volcanic activity can cause short-term climate change.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Large eruptions send ash and gases into the atmosphere. - These particles reflect sunlight away from Earth, which causes cooling, known as a volcanic winter. - Volcanic winters last only a few years. - Volcanoes also release carbon dioxide. - However, they do not release enough CO₂ to explain long-term warming.

resources.title: Explain why volcanoes are a serious natural hazard.

content.questionTitleMd: Explain why volcanoes are a serious natural hazard.
content.markScheme:
**Level 1: 1-3 marks**
Statements including limited detail

**Level 2: 4-6 marks**
More developed or linked statements

**Level 3: 7 marks**
Comprehensive and accurate statements

**Indicative content**
- Volcanoes can produce lava flows during eruptions. - Lava can destroy buildings, roads and farmland. - Volcanoes release ash clouds that can block sunlight. - Ash can damage crops and cause food shortages. - Volcanic gases, such as sulphur dioxide, can be poisonous and cause breathing problems. - Pyroclastic flows move very fast and are extremely hot, making them deadly. - Because eruptions are often sudden and unpredictable, many people’s lives are at risk.

<md>

ans = (a+b+c+d+e+f)/6
